title: Mass or Number? Periodic Law Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
In class, names are called by roll number, not by height. Every list works only when it uses the right number. Mendeleev's table ordered elements by atomic mass, and a few of them sat out of place. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) we find the number that fixed it.

You will see what the atomic number Z counts (the protons in the nucleus, and the electrons in a neutral atom), then run Henry Moseley's 1913 X-ray test on the molecule bench: metal after metal, the square root of the X-ray frequency against Z falls on one straight line, while against atomic mass the line breaks at cobalt and nickel. That gives the modern periodic law: the properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers. A worked example names element 119 the IUPAC way (Ununennium, Uue), then the exam trap about argon and potassium, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 27 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
